# Sandbox Linux

`just sandbox-linux` runs one live Claude Code session in a Linux container.
It checks that the sandbox blocks a Unix socket in a `Bash` call.
Run it before you add a `sandbox` key to the settings snippet.
It uses your login and costs money.

## What It Checks

The seccomp helper of the native Claude Code build must block a Unix socket in a sandboxed `Bash` call.
The script is `dev/sandbox/linux/run.ts`, and it runs `dev/sandbox/linux/check.sh` in the container.

The session uses these settings:

```json
{"sandbox": {"enabled": true, "failIfUnavailable": true,
  "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false, "autoAllowBashIfSandboxed": true}}
```

The prompt asks Claude to run one `socat` call to `$SSH_AUTH_SOCK`.
The socket is a fake agent of `socat` in the container, not the `ssh-agent` of the host.
A control call outside the sandbox must connect.

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | The control connects and the sandboxed call does not |
| `reached` | The sandboxed call connects |
| `unknown` | The control fails or the session gives no result |

The recipe exits with 1 for any verdict but `blocked`.

## How It Runs

1. Build the image from the image of `just docker`, with `bubblewrap` and `socat` added (`dev/sandbox/linux/Dockerfile`).
2. Read the login of the host, from the Keychain on macOS or `.credentials.json` on Linux.
3. Stop when the access token has less than `LINUX_TOKEN_MIN_MINUTES` (30) minutes left.
   A refresh in the container would make the login of the host fail.
   Run one `claude` command on the host to refresh it, then run the recipe again.
4. Run the container with `--rm`, `--privileged` (so `bwrap` can make namespaces), and `DOCKER_CPUS` CPUs.
   The login goes in on stdin, and no file of the host gets it.
5. Print the control result, each `Bash` command and result, the sandbox lines of stderr, and the verdict.

## Cost and Approval

The session uses the model `LINUX_SESSION_MODEL` (`haiku`) for one short turn of at most 3 turns.
Ask the user before each run.
The recipe does not run in `just docker`, because it needs the login of the host.
